messages:
Maria: quick follow-up on AttrV2 decisions we shipped the RFC but a few operational tradeoffs need explicit calls before we craft a rollout schedule. primary things: attribute storage shape, sampling interaction, and cost attribution guarantees.
Jason: top-line worry = unbounded cardinality from freeform attrs. if we naively put everything into columns we explode partition counts and TSDB series. we need to enforce a narrow core and an escape hatch.
Kevin: +1. also think about query ergonomics: engineers will expect to filter by model_id and route cheaply. those must be first-class. other debugging attrs can live in a blob.
Nina: proposal variant: CORE columns = tenant_id, trace_id, cost_key, model_id, route, seq_len, ts. core types are strongly typed. extend_map as gzipped json blob stored in object store with a small pointer in the row (s3://...). retrieval on demand. this keeps hot storage small.
Maria: pointer-to-blob is attractive but complicates our read path for lightweight queries. we often need to scan millions of rows for billing joins; fetching blobs would be expensive. maybe compressed in-row blob but with size cap (e.g., 2KB) and drop when exceeded.
Theo: one compromise: store top-N extension keys (hot keys) in separate narrow columns dynamically via a sidecar catalog. archive the rest in blob. sidecar keeps hot keys updateable without schema migrations.
Jason: nice. sidecar catalog needs TTL and eviction heuristics to avoid flip-flopping. also an ownership model: which service can promote a key into hot set?
Kevin: about sampling: current edge sampler drops 80% traffic and we rely on envelope attributes for billing. if enrichment adds cost_key after sampling, we lose attribution. we should consider one of: (A) require cost_key upstream, (B) move sampling downstream (post-enrich), (C) emit cheap cost-claim event as a joinable sentinel when enrichment fills cost_key, or (D) maintain a tiny sampled stream of pre-enrich raw envelopes for backfill.
Nina: operational pros/cons: (A) simplest but breaks SDKs that can't compute cost_key. (B) moves cost downstream increasing load on core pipeline. (C) seems least disruptive: enrichment emits small indexed event cost_claim{trace_id,cost_key,ts}. billing joins on that.
Maria: need to quantify join latency and storage cost for (C). if cost_claim is indexed in a compact key-value store (trace_id -> cost_key, ttl 7d) we can keep cost joins bounded.
Theo: agree. implement cost_claim in Dynamo-like store with strong read throughput; billing lookup is then O(1) at ingest. add eventual consistency markers if claim is delayed.
Kevin: alerting: metric "billing_match_rate" = percent of processed requests with cost attribution at final billing time. set SLO 99.5% for attributed tokens for committed customers. for discrepancies we run backfill.
Jason: migration plan idea: dual-write period where services write both AttrV1 and AttrV2 shapes. add server-side translation table mapping legacy keys -> canonical keys for 9 months. expose translation metrics to owners.
Nina: SDK story: publish canonical shapes and provide client-side shim that maps legacy keys locally until clients upgrade. also add an autorolling lint check in CI that flags deprecated keys.
Maria: security/compliance: we must ensure extensions can't carry PII. add validation rules in ingestion that run basic regex checks on extension top-level strings and redact high-risk patterns, logging redaction counts.
Theo: storage optimizations: for model_id and route, maintain a dictionary service that maps strings to 64-bit integers. store ints in columns to reduce storage and index bloat. keep reverse map for human queries.
Kevin: cost modeling: compute expected storage delta for extensions blob at 5%,25%,100% rollout using current payload histograms. we should gate rollout if projected monthly storage adds > 8% of current.
Jason: rollout steps: 1) finalize CORE set + type defs, 2) implement server translation map + client shim, 3) dual-write canary at 3% for 2w, monitor cardinality, billing_match_rate, and storage delta, 4) expand to 20% for 2w, then 100% with org opt-outs.
Maria: owners: Maria = CORE + rollout document, Kevin = cost_claim prototype + ingestion validation, Nina = SDK shim + deprecation lint, Jason = monitoring dashboards and cardinality alerts, Theo = dictionary service + sidecar catalog prototype. i'll open a short addendum RFC and link infra tickets.
obs-bot: created task ORG-9001 "AttrV2 operational runbook + cost_claim prototype" assigned to Maria, Kevin, Nina, Jason, Theo. :white_check_mark:
Maria: thanks everyone. i'll post the addendum in #eng-platform and ping product for SLA language.
